survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a PIRLS 2001 database user guide supplement describing national adaptations of background questionnaire items for secondary analysis. It does not provide an analytic sample, scaling, or any estimation procedure, so no student or replicate weights are specified. For users working with PIRLS 2001 background variables, the appropriate approach is to apply the PIRLS sampling/analysis weights provided in the main PIRLS 2001 international database documentation when producing population-representative estimates. This supplement focuses on questionnaire comparability (codes D/X for inclusion/exclusion of internationally comparable items) rather than on how to compute weighted statistics.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because this supplement does not analyze cognitive achievement outcomes or generate/estimate PV-based scores; it only documents how background questionnaire items were adapted or excluded by country. Missing-data handling is not reported because there is no modeling or estimation step in this document—only item-level availability/comparability information (e.g., Code D vs Code X).

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: This supplement does not define an analytic student sample. Instead, it documents item-level national adaptations and comparability for PIRLS 2001 background questionnaire variables, using country codes (D = included in the international database; X = not included due to non-administration, non-comparability, deletion, or other data problems).

data.outcome_summary: This document is a PIRLS 2001 database user guide supplement focused on documenting national adaptations of international background questionnaire items. It does not conduct any statistical analysis, machine learning, or achievement scaling; instead, it provides item-level information (question text abbreviation, variable names, and per-country documentation) to help researchers judge whether background variables are internationally comparable for secondary analyses. Countries are coded as D when national data are included in the international database and X when the item is not included due to non-administration, non-comparability, deletion, or other data problems. The supplement also clarifies that it does not cover simple recodes made to achieve comparability (e.g., option reversals), which users must handle separately when constructing analysis datasets. As a result, there are no model performance metrics or predictive effects to interpret for policy.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a non-empirical documentation supplement rather than an empirical study: it contains questionnaire item comparability metadata, not an analysis with an analytic sample, PVs, missing-data strategy, or ML model evaluation. Therefore, fields such as total_students, per-country n_students, and main_findings are not applicable. The presence of many country codes reflects item availability documentation rather than a modeled dataset.
